Threat: Anonymous download / exfiltration of customer report data
Vulnerability: Bucket and account-level Block Public Access disabled; bucket policy allows s3:GetObject to Principal:*
Existing Controls: Post-fix (verified): public-read policy removed; bucket and account Block Public Access re-enabled. Anonymous GET now returns HTTP 403.
Scoring Rationale: L5: verified anonymously readable; open buckets are found by scanners within hours. I5: Confidential customer data, contractual and breach-notification exposure. Residual risk Low (see 06-remediation-plan/implemented-fixes.md).

Threat: Compromise of the web host leads to theft of admin credentials and full account takeover
Vulnerability: Role has AdministratorAccess and is attached to an internet-facing host that also exposes SSH (M-01) and allows IMDSv1 (M-05); role credentials are retrievable without an application vulnerability
Existing Controls: Instance currently stopped (operational state, not a control).
Scoring Rationale: L4: SSH open to the internet plus IMDSv1 means a foothold yields role credentials directly. I5: AdministratorAccess equals total account compromise.

Threat: Unauthorised login via credential brute-force or stolen key giving a foothold on the web host
Existing Controls: EC2 key-pair auth only; OS password auth disabled by default on AL2023; instance stopped.
Scoring Rationale: L3: management port is continuously scanned, but key-only auth makes successful entry less likely. I4: foothold on the host carrying the admin role (feeds R-02).

Threat: An SSRF-class vulnerability in a workload yields unauthenticated retrieval of instance role credentials
Vulnerability: IMDSv2 not required (IMDSv1 token-optional); account-level default not enforced
Existing Controls: Post-fix: IMDSv2 set to Required on the instance (HttpTokens=required, applied). IMDSv1 requests now rejected.
Scoring Rationale: L3: requires an SSRF-class flaw, but IMDSv1 makes exploitation trivial once present. I4: leaks the attached role credentials (currently admin). Fix is distinct from R-02 (enforce IMDSv2 vs scope the role). Residual: R-02/R-03 still open, so host compromise by other means would still expose the role.

Threat: Credential phishing or password reuse leads to unauthorised console access as an analyst
Vulnerability: Console password enabled with no MFA device
Existing Controls: Permissions scoped to S3 read-only via the meridian-analysts group; password reset required at next sign-in.
Scoring Rationale: L3: phishing is common once a password leaks. I3: read-only access, but AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess can read every bucket including customer-reports (Confidential); no write or escalation path.

Threat: A low-privilege actor escalates to administrator by attaching the admin role to an instance and reading its credentials
Threat Source: External attacker with Callum-v2 credentials / malicious insider
Vulnerability: Inline policies AltPermsEC2 and EC2Perm grant ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute, ec2:CreateLaunchTemplateVersion and ec2:StartInstances/StopInstances; an AdministratorAccess instance role exists in the account
Scoring Rationale: L2: requires Callum-v2 to be compromised first (R-05 raises this) and knowledge of the technique. I5: results in full administrator access.

Threat: Compromise or misuse of root credentials gives unrecoverable full account control
Vulnerability: Root protected by virtual (TOTP) MFA only, not a phishing-resistant hardware device; root is also used for routine operations rather than reserved for break-glass
Existing Controls: Virtual MFA enabled on root (verified: iam_root_mfa_enabled PASS); strong unique root password assumed.
Scoring Rationale: L1: password plus virtual MFA is a strong barrier; residual risk is the absence of phishing-resistant hardware MFA plus the practice of using root for day-to-day work. I5: root cannot be constrained by IAM.

Threat: Data-at-rest exposure via snapshot sharing, volume detachment or backend media handling
Threat Source: Malicious insider / attacker with EC2 permissions
Vulnerability: Volumes vol-0a3126a768fc6238a and vol-04097aa795bc6cbd4 unencrypted; account default EBS encryption disabled
Scoring Rationale: L2: needs prior AWS access or an unusual disclosure path. I3: the DB host would hold Confidential data; no account-layer encryption or key segregation.

Threat: Network-based intrusion or exfiltration cannot be detected or investigated
Threat Source: N/A - control gap that amplifies other threats
Scoring Rationale: L3: an incident needing this evidence is plausible given the other exposures. I3: slows and limits response; not a direct loss.

Threat: Malicious activity (root use, policy or security-group changes, failed logins) goes unnoticed until damage is done
Vulnerability: CloudTrail not delivered to CloudWatch Logs; no metric filters or alarms; no GuardDuty
Existing Controls: CloudTrail recording (multi-region, log-file validation) - logs exist but nothing watches them.
Scoring Rationale: L3: given the exposures above, triggering activity is plausible. I3: increases dwell time and blast radius of other risks. Partly a known lab trade-off (Step 7).

Threat: Leaked or committed static keys used for unauthorised API access
Vulnerability: Long-lived access keys with broad service permissions; no move to short-lived or role-based credentials
Scoring Rationale: L3: static keys routinely leak via commits, laptops and CI logs. I3: broad but not admin on their own (see R-06 for escalation).

Threat: Weak or reused console passwords guessed or brute-forced
Vulnerability: Password policy below CIS baseline: length under 14, no reuse-24, no expiry, missing complexity requirements
Scoring Rationale: L2: console throttling limits online guessing, but a weak policy widens exposure. I3: depends on the accounts it protects.

Threat: Prolonged exposure window if key material is ever compromised
Vulnerability: Automatic annual rotation disabled on the meridian CMK
Existing Controls: Key policy limits use to CloudTrail; single-purpose key.
Scoring Rationale: L1: key compromise is rare and there is no current indicator. I3: encrypts the audit log. Quick win.

Threat: Forgotten roles with unknown trust and permissions become an unmonitored attack path
Vulnerability: Leftover roles DemoEC2 and aws-ec2-spot-fleet-tagging-role - no owner, purpose unknown, no confused-deputy conditions
Scoring Rationale: L2: unclear exposure. I2: no evidence of high privilege, but unknown by definition. Review and delete.

Threat: Object tampering or deletion; plaintext interception; no forensic record of bucket access
Vulnerability: No aws:SecureTransport (HTTPS-only) policy, no object versioning, no server access logging on either bucket
Existing Controls: CloudTrail log-file validation (trail integrity); SSE-KMS on the CloudTrail bucket.
Scoring Rationale: L2: needs existing access or a network position. I3: integrity of the CloudTrail log bucket matters for investigations.

Threat: Credential phishing or password reuse leads to unauthorised console access as the build / admin user
Vulnerability: Console password enabled with no MFA device
Scoring Rationale: L3: phishing is common once a password leaks. I4: broad standing access plus a direct escalation path to administrator (see R-06). Split from R-05 - different user, different permissions.
